cells.tense: Right now you choose a direction with your hands open rather than gripped.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: Take what you've chosen to carry, and give it the next stretch of the day with no fresh ruling — no plan forward, no re-check on whether it stays. Carry it, and let time do its work.
cells.core:
You can hold something and not brace around it. When a direction matters, you have the whole move — the choice, the grip, the hours it will take — and you can carry it loosely. That isn't coldness. It's holding a thing the size it actually is instead of the size your worry gives it.

One piece stays with you after the decision: you make the call once, then test it again and again in the hours that follow. That's carrying it, then clutching it. The call you already made, on the thing in your hands — give it a stretch of time beyond where you'd usually go back over it. Not forever; an afternoon. See how it sits when nobody, including you, is arguing with it.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry a decision without gripping it.
cells.verb: choosing one direction and letting the others close behind you

cells.tense: In the weeks ahead you will force the outcome, then force it again, and call it direction.
cells.act: see the whole pattern you are standing inside
cells.ask: Catch yourself pushing something toward a close — the extra follow-up, the third re-check. Stop there and take in the whole shape: where it began, where it is, where you sit inside it. Then let the shape rest.
cells.core:
You are running the future before it arrives. The direction is real, but it has gone tight — working the outcome in advance, bracing at a picture you can't write yet. In your hands this looks like preparation, thoroughness. It's white-knuckling, and the person on the other side of it can feel the squeeze even when nothing is said.

Stand back inside it for a moment. Find the whole pattern you're standing inside — where the thing began, where it is now, where you are in the middle of it. You hold the picture of where you're trying to arrive, and you don't hold one of what's actually here. Take the picture back far enough to include the one moving, at this moment. What you see clearer, you stop having to push.
cells.sheetLine: You force tomorrow so hard today can't arrive.

cells.tense: What has been decided for you, you are still standing in — and the moment to answer it has passed.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Handle one small task in your own manner. No notice taken, no reason offered, no proof. Do it quietly, as it comes naturally, and then stop. That is all it asks.
cells.core:
The direction is there. It just isn't running. Somewhere along the line the decision stopped feeling like yours, and you stopped arriving. The hands have gone still while the moment keeps passing, and the smaller the moment, the louder the case for letting it pass.

One small task, handled your own way — that is the whole ask. Not a big decision, not a plan. The manner you already bring to small things, once, without announcing it. Energy follows an action that is actually yours; it doesn't follow logic, or a good reason why it ought to. Leave the reason. Do the thing the way you do it, and find out whether your own name is still attached to it.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped arriving in a life that kept moving.

cells.tense: You are steering all of it right now, and by your own account the wheel isn't there.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Find something you did this week that didn't get counted as a choice — the task that got done because it was yours. Say one plain line about it, in your own words. Not why. Not should. Just what you did.
cells.core:
You have been directing things for a long time. The choices are real and steady: the small ones, the ones that keep people held, the ones made without a pause because habit does the work. There's no fight in you about it. The only quiet thing is who is doing it — the account you carry doesn't include the one holding the pen.

Take a thing you did this week and didn't count as a decision. Put one line about it in your own words, plain, not important-sounding. The line is for you, not for anyone else. With it in your hands, choosing on purpose may get easier — not because you'd stopped, but because the one doing it will recognize their own handwriting.
cells.sheetLine: You've been choosing without counting the choices as yours.
